newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end "sleepy summer day" lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end "sleepy summer day" lower.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries withstood a stream of negative factors to end marginally lower on Tuesday.
Losses were tempered as each time prices slipped, buying emerged.
The 30-year bond closed at 100-15/32, down 5/32, while its yield inched up to 6.59 percent from 6.58 percent.
Activity was dominated by "day traders," who were mostly position-squaring, traders said.
"It was a typical sleepy, summer day," said Bill Kirby, co-head government bond trader at Prudential Securities Inc.
According to GovPX, some $55 billion traded by 1500 EDT/1900 GMT. Most of the action took place in outstanding five- and 10-year notes at more than $5 billion each.
The light activity confined Treasuries to tight ranges. "People are waiting for something to happen," Kirby said.
In the absence of key economic data, technical factors weighed heavily on the market, players noted.

Early in the session, talk of Argentina issuing a 30-year bond to redeem outstanding Brady debt pressured Treasuries, along with a huge amount of corporate and agency supply, as well as the release of a mortgage bid list to dealers.
Meanwhile, with many players viewing the market as at or near its peak, some profit-taking was reported.

Still, "The market had a fair amount of people who wanted to buy dips," said Rich Bodkin, head of the government bond desk at First Chicago Capital Markets Inc. He added that Treasuries slowly inched higher until late in the session when "locals" that had become long booked some profits.
"There really is not much to talk about," Bodkin said. "There was little interest in the market today."
Indeed, Treasuries even shrugged off the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond survey for June, which showed a price rise.

The most noise in the market took place in the Treasury inflation protected securities (TIPS) sector, where the market was getting ready for the first-ever auction of five-year TIPS notes on Wednesday. The Treasury will sell $8.0 billion of the securities at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT on Wednesday.
The when-issued five-year TIPS note was, as traders said, "hammered," rising more than 10 basis points from late Monday.
In late trading, the when issued five-year TIPS was at 3.645 percent, up from 3.54 percent on Monday. The 10-year TIPS rose to 3.685 percent from 3.61 percent.
Volume in the five-year TIPS was a robust $400 million, while 10-year TIPS volume was $268 million, GovPX reported.

Traders said with inflation at low levels and virtually no concerns of a pick-up, TIPS' demand appeared slim. Therefore, the market needed to build in heavy concessions, which, traders noted, still does not guarantee a successful auction.
"It looks like the five-year TIPS may have to struggle," said Bodkin.
Added Kirby: "There is low demand for inflation protection. People are still uncertain how TIPS will trade in extreme circumstances."

In late trading, the two-year note was at 100-5/32, down 1/32, to yield 5.91 percent. The five-year note was down 1/32 at 100-11/32 with a yield of 6.17 percent. The 10-year note closed down 2/32 at 102-19/32 to yield 6.27 percent.
The three-month bill was up two basis points at 4.97 percent. The six-month bill was up six basis points at 5.08 percent and the year-bill was unchanged at 5.24 percent.
